summaries.summary: The hierarchical model is compared against three systems, reporting each paper's best performing model results.
Wiseman BIBREF10 is a standard encoder-decoder system with copy mechanism.
Li BIBREF28 is a standard encoder-decoder with delayed copy mechanism using placeholders replaced by salient records extracted by a pointer network.
Puduppully-plan BIBREF12 uses two steps: a standard encoder-decoder generates a plan, then another generates text from this plan.
Puduppully-updt BIBREF13 is a standard encoder-decoder with a module updating record representations during generation via a gated recurrent network.
The importance of input structure is tested by training different variants of the proposed architecture.
Flat feeds input sequentially to the encoder, loses hierarchy, uses standard attention, and uses a Transformer instead of an RNN unlike Wiseman.
Hierarchical-kv is the full hierarchical model with traditional hierarchical attention over records computed on the full record encoding, as in equation (SECREF16).
Hierarchical-k is the full hierarchical model with key-guided hierarchical attention over records computed only on record key representations, as in equation (DISPLAY_FORM17).

Implementation details specify decoder hyperparameters, two-layers multi-head self-attention with two heads, embedding size 20 for 39 record keys, size 300, dropout 0.5, batch size 64, 25K updates, last 5 checkpoints at every 1K updates, Adam BIBREF37, initial learning rate 0.001 reduced by half every 10K steps, beam size 5, OpenNMT-py BIBREF38, and code at https://github.com/KaijuML/data-to-text-hierarchical.

RotoWire testset results in Table TABREF25 report mean scores over ten runs with standard deviations, baselines BIBREF12, BIBREF13, BIBREF10, variants, and oracle metrics, with gold descriptions obtaining 100% except RG, IE failing 4% of the time, and RG-# an absolute count.
Comparing Flat, Hierarchical-k, and Hierarchical-kv shows Flat lower results, such as BLEU 16.7 vs. 17.5 for Flat and Hierarchical-k, suggesting hierarchy effectiveness.
Hierarchical-k performs slightly better than Hierarchical-kv in all metrics except CS-R%, with sharp attention on (PTS_QTR1, 26) versus distributed PTS_QTR records.

Table TABREF25 shows scenarios significantly higher in BLEU, with Hierarchical-k reaching 17.5 vs. 16.5 against the best baseline, while generated texts still contain incorrect facts and hallucinations.
Specific statements regarding all baselines are outlined.

Hierarchical models achieve significantly better scores than Wiseman on all metrics, with RG# 16.83 vs. 17.31, Wiseman 75.62% precision and 22.25 records, and Hierarchical-k 89.46% precision and 23.66 total mentions.
Flat and Wiseman differ by bi-LSTM vs. Transformer, with Flat obtaining higher BLEU 16.7 vs. 14.5 and accurate RG-P% mentions included in gold descriptions as CS-R%.
Hierarchical models outperform Li and Puduppully-plan on BLEU and all qualitative metrics, while Puduppully-plan reaches 34.28 mentions on average.
Puduppully-updt improves Content Ordering (CO) and RG-P%, but Hierarchical-k obtains slightly better Content Selection (CS), with Puduppully-updt RG-# score of 30.11.
The scenarios use 14 millions parameters compared to baselines ranging from 23 to 45 millions, outlining effectiveness of structure encoding.

The proposed hierarchical encoder leverages structure, synergizes with hierarchical attention, outperforms competitive RotoWire baselines in BLEU and qualitative metrics, but can still produce erroneous facts or hallucinations.
The H2020 project AI4EU (825619) partially supports Laure Soulier and Patrick Gallinari.
